question.prompt: How many zeros are at the end of the product \[ \begin{aligned} &25 \times 25 \times 25 \times 25 \\ &\quad {}\times 25 \times 25 \times 25 \\ &\quad {}\times 8 \times 8 \times 8? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.explanation:
Multiplying by \(10\) appends a zero, and each factor of \(10\) can be made by pairing a \(2\) with a \(5\).

Each of the seven factors of \(25\) supplies two factors of \(5\), giving \(14\) altogether. Each of the three factors of \(8\) supplies three factors of \(2\), giving \(9\) altogether.

We can therefore form nine pairs, leaving five factors of \(5\). Thus
\[
\text{product}=5^5\times10^9=3125\times10^9.
\]
Since \(3125\) does not end in zero, the product ends in exactly \(9\) zeros, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Pair factors of 2 and 5
